summary: VBS / Credential Guard enabled during imaging blocks Windows Hello facial enrollment post-provisioning
description:
Issue summary:
When devices are provisioned from the new SCCM/Intune hybrid task sequence (TS-2026-v2) VBS (Virtualization Based Security) and Credential Guard are being left enabled. End-users cannot complete Windows Hello (Facial/IR camera) enrollment after first sign-in. Enrollment UI reports a generic error and returns immediately.

Impact:
- New hires and reimages unable to enroll face unlock; slows time-to-productive for ~12% of provisioning runs in staging so far.
- Manual workaround required by IT to disable VBS or re-run provisioning which delays handover.

Environment:
- Imaging task sequence: TS-2026-v2 (SCCM -> Intune autopilot handoff)
- Affected OS: Windows 11 22H2 corporate image (customized with Defender ATP, VBS policy bundle)
- Regions: staging-us-east, small sample in prod-us-west reported by 2 users
- Affected models: Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 10, Dell Latitude 7440

Steps to reproduce:
1) Boot device to SCCM PXE and run TS-2026-v2 provisioning sequence
2) Device is joined and Intune enrollment runs post-OOBE
3) Complete out-of-box experience and sign in with corp account
4) Attempt to set up Windows Hello Face (IR camera)

Observed behavior:
- Windows Hello enrollment fails immediately with an error (translated UI message: "Can't set up your camera right now")
- Event Viewer: Microsoft-Windows-User Device Registration / Operational shows Error 0x80090016 and TPM access denied messages.
- System logs show Device Guard / Credential Guard service active and VBS reported enabled (Platform Configuration Manager trace).

Expected behavior:
- Windows Hello enrollment should succeed for supported hardware without requiring VBS to be disabled during provisioning.

Temporary workaround:
- IT Support: Disable VBS/Credential Guard using the bcdedit toggle (bcdedit /set hypervisorlaunchtype off) and reboot; then re-run Hello enrollment. Alternatively reimage using legacy TS that does not enable VBS. Both are manual and disruptive.

Attachments:
- Screenshots of enrollment error, exported Event Viewer snippet, SCCM task sequence logs (smsts.log) excerpt.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Jenna Liu: Ticket created after two repros in staging. Attached smsts.log and event snippets.

2026-03-10 11:05 - Ravi Menon: I can repro locally on a Dell 7440. Confirmed VBS flagged as enabled in registry (HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\DeviceGuard). Collecting full kernel boot logs and bcdedit output.

2026-03-11 08:43 - SRE (Marco Rivera): Noted SCCM TS step 'Apply-Corp-Defender-Profile' now applies Device Guard policy package. That step was added in TS-2026-v2 to harden endpoints; looks like it also enables VBS by default on supported hardware.

2026-03-12 14:20 - Security (Aisha Patel): VBS is desirable for threat protection, but blocking provisioning is bad. Propose we ship a temporary change to the TS to defer applying Device Guard until post-provisioning/first-login so Hello can enroll, and then enable VBS after enrollment completes.

2026-03-13 10:02 - Ravi Menon: Pushed a test TS version (TS-2026-v2a) that defers Device Guard. Running 10 machines in staging; 9/10 now successfully enroll Windows Hello. Need engineering sign-off to roll to prod.
investigation_notes: Collected smsts.log, setupact.log and Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-Boot logs from failing machines.
Observed registry keys set by TS: DeviceGuard_EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity=1 and LsaCfgFlags modified for Credential Guard.
Windows Hello enrollment uses user-mode access to TPM APIs; Credential Guard blocks certain legacy TPM provisioning flows until user-mode virtualization is available.
Disabling hypervisor launch via bcdedit allows enrollment to proceed immediately (consistent repro).
TS change added in PR infra/pull/4123 to harden devices; that PR did not include Hello enrollment regression tests.
Risk assessment: deferring Device Guard to post-enroll reduces short-term security posture for 5-15 minutes per device but avoids manual IT interventions at scale.
resolution: Workaround implemented in staging: TS-2026-v2a defers Device Guard policy until after first sign-in. Verified 9/10 success in staging. Action items: 1) Update TS template to include conditional Device Guard activation post-Hello enrollment. 2) Add automated provisioning test that validates Windows Hello enrollment on supported SKUs. 3) Security to approve post-enroll Device Guard enablement window. 4) Plan controlled rollout to prod next week.
next_steps: Security review and sign-off on deferred VBS approach (owner: Aisha Patel)
Add Windows Hello enrollment check to provisioning CI (owner: Ravi Menon)
Roll TS-2026-v2a to prod canary (50 devices) after approval (owner: Ops)
